newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Premier says Discovery not undervalued.
newsitem.headline: Premier says Discovery not undervalued.

text.p: U.K.-based Premier Oil Plc said on Wednesday that its 80 cent per share bid for Discovery Petroleum NL did not continue to undervalue the company as claimed by the target firm.

"The facts do not support your directors claim that, because 80 cents is below the mid-point of the independent experts valuation, our revised offer undervalues Discovery's shares," Premier chairman Charles Jamieson said in a letter to Discovery shareholders. Premier raised its bid from 70 cents last week.
Discovery shares ended one cent lower at 80 cents but reached a year's high of 82 cents during the day.

"You should be aware that shareholders have accepted a price below the mid-point of the valuation range in every successful takeover in the oil and gas sector since 1993 where an independent expert has valued the target company," Jamieson said. "In 67 percent of these cases, shareholders accepted a price below the low point of the range," he said.
In a report prepared for Discovery, merchant bank Grant Samuel valued Discovery shares at between 77 and 95 cents each.
Analysts have said Oil Search Ltd, which has a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery, could announce a rival bid soon.
Oil Search, which is based in the Papua New Guinea capital of Port Moresby, paid 75 cents per share for its stake and last week began due diligence on Discovery's portfolio.
Oil Search has said it was attracted to Discovery's assets, particularly in Southeast Asia where it has an 18.75 percent stake in Indonesia's Kakap gas fields.
